history.period: attributed to the Jaintia kings; some sources say 13th century (verify — the neighbouring Durga temple is dated 16th-17th century, so a 13th-century date is unconfirmed)
history.summary: IDENTITY UNCERTAIN/PROVISIONAL: a distinct Shiva shrine stands within walking distance of the Nartiang Durga Temple (town corrected from CSV 'Nongpoh' to Nartiang, West Jaintia Hills; real state is MEGHALAYA, not the CSV town entry). It has a real web footprint but no dedicated official listing: travel and temple sources confirm a nearby Shiva shrine holding figurines of Shiva and other deities, vintage iron cannons, and offerings of fruit and kwai (betel nut with paan). The indusscrolls account calls it one of the oldest temples in Meghalaya and reports that devotees wish to install a Shiv lingam, which local Christians oppose — treated as an unverified single-source report, flag. A shrine in the area is also referred to as the 'Sahmai Mandir' where cannons are displayed; it is unclear whether that is this Shiva shrine — flag as ambiguous. Renovation a few decades ago; sparsely visited except at Shivaratri. If the CSV intends the Sahmai/khasi-sacred shrine rather than a Shaiva temple, this record may need reclassification.

name: Shiva Temple, Nartiang
town_description: Nartiang is a historic village in the West Jaintia Hills district, about 65 km from Shillong, once the summer capital of the Jaintia Kingdom. It is famous for the Nartiang monoliths — tall stone pillars, the tallest about 27 feet, called the 'Stonehenge of the North East' — and for its ancient Durga and Shiva temples.

travel.airport: Shillong Airport, about 60 km (approximate; Guwahati Airport about 170 km)
travel.railway: Guwahati Railway Station, about 140 km (approximate; no rail line in the Jaintia Hills)
travel.road: About 65 km from Shillong by road via Jowai; the shrine is within walking distance of the Nartiang Durga Temple
